..$comment: COUPLING (#27): consumers install a version-keyed cache of this plugin (#6) — a whole-repo checkout of the tagged commit — so a fix to anything they run only reaches them once a release is cut here. This repo squash-merges, which makes the PR *title* the commit release-please reads on main — so the guarantee depends on that title carrying a releasable type. scripts/release-title-gate.sh enforces it in CI for PRs touching shipped plugin content, which it defines by exclusion: everything except the development-only paths in its NON_SHIPPED list (docs/, tests/, evals/, reviews/, samples/, .github/, .claude/ and the root markdown). It was originally scoped to skills/** alone; #55 widened it, because scripts/, commands/, templates/, hooks/ and requirements.json are equally install-time. Two paths are gated despite living under an excluded directory, because a shipped skill resolves them by name out of the install cache: tests/xunit-v3/apply-transform.py (its version constants land in every migrated csproj) and docs/backlog.md (skills/followups mandates it). Change the merge strategy (or that script's releasable set) and the guarantee has to be re-established somewhere else. NOTE the carve-out that protects THIS file's own siblings: the release PR release-please opens is titled `chore(main): release X.Y.Z` and touches exactly .claude-plugin/plugin.json + .release-please-manifest.json + CHANGELOG.md, and `chore` is not releasable — so gating it would mean no release PR could ever merge. The gate exempts it on BOTH its title and a changeset that is a subset of those three files, deliberately not by excluding the paths: plugin.json is shipped (it declares mcpServers/hooks), so a human `chore:` edit to it is still refused. Two known holes the gate does NOT close, because it only sees the pull_request event: overriding the squash subject at merge time (`gh pr merge --squash --subject …`, or editing the message in GitHub's merge box) lands a different commit than the one that was gated, and a direct push to main is never gated at all. JSON carries no comments; this key is inert — release-please reads named fields only, and the config schema allows extra keys inside a package entry.
